description: We are CosmoTensor, a team of 4 Computer Science & Data Science students passionate about decoding Earth system trends with NASA open data! Our core stack includes Python, pandas, machine learning, and interactive visualization tools (Streamlit/Plotly). We’re tackling "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" to uncover actionable climate insights. Looking for collaborative teammates skilled in coding, data storytelling, or UI design to build something impactful!
summary: Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive web application developed by Team CosmoTensor for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Be An Earth System Trend Detective!").We developed a Python- and Streamlit-powered platform that streams live meteorological parameters—specifically surface temperature (T2M) and precipitation (PRECTOTCORR)—directly from the NASA POWER API for any user-selected global coordinates and timeframe.The application addresses the challenge by automating the complete data-to-insight pipeline: it extracts raw time-series data, resamples it into monthly averages, visualizes long-term changes using OLS regression trendlines, and computes rigorous statistical significance ($p$-values) to instantly determine whether a regional climate shift is statistically significant.This is important because understanding localized environmental trends is vital for regional resource management, agricultural planning, and climate awareness. By bridging complex data science with an intuitive, accessible interface, our tool empowers researchers, students, and citizens to decode Earth's changing systems and make data-driven environmental discoveries effortlessly.
details:
• What it does & How it works: An interactive web app that fetches live meteorological data (surface temperature and precipitation) from the NASA POWER API for any user-selected global coordinates. It automatically processes time-series data, resamples it into monthly averages, plots OLS regression trendlines, and computes $p$-values to evaluate statistical significance.
  • Benefits: Provides instant access to NASA data without complex scripts, automates statistical rigor to separate natural variance from real climate shifts, and offers an intuitive interface for all users.
  • Intended Impact: Democratizes climate data analysis, empowering regional planners, educators, and citizens to understand local environmental changes and support climate resilience.
  • Tech Stack: Python, Streamlit, Pandas, SciPy, Statsmodels, Plotly, NASA POWER API, and GitHub.
  • Creativity: Bridges heavy scientific datasets with consumer-grade interactivity, packaging live API streaming, monthly resampling, and hypothesis testing into a seamless point-and-click dashboard.
  • Key Factors Considered: Ensured statistical accuracy via robust regression testing, optimized performance for smooth real-time rendering, and prioritized a clean, accessible user experience.
dataRefs: NASA POWER API (Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources)
projectRefs: Python Scientific Stack (Pandas, SciPy, Statsmodels, Plotly)
